title: Review: jmap-mail-types
notes:
Maintainer risk: LOW — No correctness bugs. One P1 maintainer-burden issue (macro discoverability). Wire types are spec-faithful. All types are non-exhaustive. No unsafe, no async leakage.
Confidence: 5% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: none — all findings are elegance/readability. Uncertainty driven by: not reading the full RFC 8621 text inline. Would raise confidence if: ran against a real JMAP server response fixture.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — No unsafe, no unwrap in production code, no gratuitous clones. Main concerns: (1) MailboxRole duplicates the macro pattern from submission.rs; (2) two string-type fields (comparator property, keyword values) could be newtypes for safety. These are real but non-blocking.
Rust idiom confidence: 10% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: the Keyword newtype suggestion (may be over-engineering for a wire-types crate). Uncertainty driven by: did not trace every caller usage pattern.
